body: Wednesday, July 22 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed under Chair Warsh has held rates steady, with rhetoric explicitly acknowledging "prices are too high" — a hawkish hold posture. The 10Y yield has climbed to 4.65% (+16 bps vs 4W), while the 2Y sits at 4.26% (prior close, +2 bps vs 4W), producing a +37 bps curve — positive but still flat by historical standards, 10 bps steeper than four weeks ago. Inflation cooled in June per the latest data, but oil's 17.9% surge over four weeks is re-igniting pass-through concerns. VIX at 16.78 (↓13.9%) signals equity complacency despite geopolitical escalation with Iran.

New / Most Important: US-Iran military strikes have driven WTI to 86.30 (↑17.9% vs 4W), and bond yields rose explicitly on the oil-inflation transmission channel per market commentary. The S&P 500 at 7521.79 (↑2.1%) has held up, but leadership has narrowed — Nasdaq 100 is actually down 0.7% vs 4W while the S&P grinds higher, suggesting mega-cap concentration around earnings catalysts (Alphabet, Tesla reporting today). A popular crypto firm filed for Chapter 11 after a token collapse, adding to digital-asset credit stress.

Playbook ✓: AI capex narrative continues to dominate equity flows — SMCI surging, Astera Labs ripping on infrastructure spend, Meta in talks for a $10B Anthropic deal. Big Tech earnings as the dominant near-term catalyst is textbook mid-cycle behavior.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The oil shock is structurally different this time. With the US now an active belligerent in the Iran conflict rather than a passive sanctions enforcer, the supply-disruption tail risk is fatter than markets are pricing at VIX 16.78. The growth pulse confirms this is a supply-shock narrative rather than a demand-led commodity rally: euro-zone banks are tightening credit access on war fears and China's June new loans missed forecasts. If Strait of Hormuz risk escalates, the Fed faces a stagflationary bind — they cannot cut into an oil-driven inflation impulse, but higher yields will stress the fiscal trajectory given elevated debt servicing costs. The complacency regime (VIX in the teens while a shooting war intensifies) is the most dangerous divergence on the board right now. Watch for a violent VIX re-pricing if Iran retaliates against US energy infrastructure or shipping lanes.

Macro Stance: Eurozone inflation printed at 2.8%, prompting active debate about whether the ECB should pause its easing cycle. The euro has strengthened above 1.1400 on hawkish ECB expectations, even amid US-Iran tensions that would normally favor USD safe-haven flows. The Q2 bank lending survey was released, providing fresh credit-impulse data.

New / Most Important: The ECB rate decision is tomorrow (Jul 23). Market pricing and commentary suggest hawkish expectations — a hold or pause rather than a cut — given inflation at 2.8% remains above target. The euro's resilience above 1.14 reflects capital flows positioning for rate divergence favoring Europe. The fresh bank lending survey from Q2 will inform whether credit conditions support the tightening bias. Canada's 50% tariff escalation headlines add to the global trade fragmentation backdrop affecting European exporters.

Playbook ✓: ECB pausing near terminal rate with inflation sticky above 2% is consensus. Euro strength is the expected corollary.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The euro holding gains *despite* a hot geopolitical war that historically sends flows to USD is notable. This may reflect a structural shift: if the US is the aggressor in a Middle East conflict, the dollar's safe-haven premium erodes because the US is the *source* of geopolitical risk rather than a refuge from it. European capital may be staying home rather than fleeing to Treasuries. Watch DXY for confirmation.

Macro Stance: Loan prime rates were held for a 14th consecutive month (The Business Times, [Jul 20]) despite the second-quarter growth miss (Sharecast, [Jul 20]), and the market now eyes a rate-cut window near the end of the third quarter (BigGo Finance, [Jul 21]). Until then the PBOC's emphasis is the currency: it sees a stable yuan amid two-way fluctuations (State Council Information Office, [Jul 16]) and is moving to deepen offshore yuan liquidity (Caixin, [Jul 16]); the yuan weakened slightly on the fixing (BusinessToday Malaysia, [Jul 17]) and UOB sees an upside bias below 6.7820 (TMGM, [Jul 20]). Prices are the wrong mix: June CPI rose only 1% (chinadailyhk, [Jul 8]) and slowed more than forecast (Bloomberg, [Jul 8]), while PPI climbed 4.1% (BigGo Finance, [Jul 8]) to a near four-year high that squeezes manufacturers (Reuters, [Jul 8]).

PMIs & Activity: The surveys and the hard data point in different directions. The June official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 and the non-manufacturing PMI to 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]); the private gauge capped the strongest factory quarter since late 2020 (Reuters, [Jun 30]). Yet second-quarter GDP growth weakened to 4.3%, below the official target range (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]). June industrial output rose 5.3% y/y and retail sales returned to growth (BusinessLine, [Jul 15]), but retail sales of consumer goods were up just 1.3% in the first half (Ecns.cn, [Jul 15]), infrastructure investment turned negative (BigGo Finance, [Jul 19]) and the car market heads for its worst year since 2021 (CNBC, [Jul 20]). Even Shanghai's 5.6% beat comes with a two-speed recovery (SCMP, [Jul 21]); Trivium reads the miss as a deepening split between tech exports and domestic demand ([Jul 21]), with June exports up 27% y/y (Reuters, [Jul 13]).

Credit Impulse: Credit is the weak link. June new loans missed forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]) and overall credit growth undershot as the PBOC flagged a "new normal" (Caixin, [Jul 16]). Household loans decreased by 366.8 billion yuan in the first half (36Kr, [Jul 17]), and record consumer defaults undermine the push to boost spending (Reuters, [Jul 15]). Read: with households repaying and private firms not borrowing, the impulse rests on state-directed financing.

Property: Prices are stabilising at the top while capital keeps leaving. June new home prices fell at a slower pace, though Reuters doubts a recovery ([Jul 14]), and first-tier prices extended a 4-month rebound (SCMP, [Jul 15]). But property investment slumped 18% y/y in January–June (The Standard, [Jul 15]) and KKR and AEW seek to sell China property assets at steep losses (Bloomberg, [Jul 20]). Developer survival still runs through state shareholders: Vanke secured a 519 million yuan loan from Shenzhen Metro at 2.29% (BigGo Finance, [Jul 21]), while Beijing curbs new bond sales by indebted LGFVs (Bloomberg, [Jul 15]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing vowed to achieve its annual growth target (Bloomberg, [Jul 20]) and the premier chaired a State Council executive meeting (Macau Business, [Jul 21]), but the toolkit is still plans and projects: the first five-year consumption plan (State Council Information Office, [Jul 15]) and faster state-backed projects to avoid broad stimulus (Reuters, [Jul 16]), even as the FT says leaders are zeroing in on the need for stimulus ([Jul 18]). At the margin support is being withdrawn, with a key tax break on lithium EV batteries ending (Caixin, [Jul 20]). On trade, EU lawmakers arrived for high-stakes talks (SCMP, [Jul 21]) and the foreign minister discussed the trade balance with them (Reuters, [Jul 21]) as the yuan draws scrutiny in Europe (Bloomberg, [Jul 21]) and Paris and Berlin present a united front (SCMP, [Jul 20]). A new US sanctions bill threatens a 100% tariff on buyers of Russian oil, China included (The Independent, [Jul 16]).

Markets & Flows: The rescue has broadened. After the national team bought shares worth $9bn (FT, [Jul 20]), Beijing added record inflows into a tech ETF (Bloomberg, [Jul 21]) and long-term buying by state-backed insurers (SCMP, [Jul 21]). Hong Kong semiconductor stocks surged over 11% (BigGo Finance, [Jul 21]) and Zhipu jumped 37% as it builds a giant data centre on Chinese chips (SCMP, [Jul 21]), though the Hang Seng closed down 0.04% (Moomoo, [Jul 21]). Breakingviews warns the national team faces a risky tech challenge (Reuters, [Jul 21]); Citi has upgraded China to overweight (The Standard, [Jul 20]).

New / Most Important: The market rescue has become AI industrial policy. Beijing seeks to rescue AI stocks without fueling a bubble (Bloomberg, [Jul 21]) while considering export controls on AI technologies, including barring local companies from using TSMC (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]). Set beside the NVIDIA-China export restriction debate in the US, which Cramer frames as national security, both sides are now fencing AI supply chains. For China that concentrates state capital in the one sector that is growing, while household credit shrinks and property investment falls; it raises valuations in tech without raising the domestic demand the Q2 miss exposed.

Playbook ✓: Rate hold, managed yuan, state support for equities and stimulus by plan rather than by cash are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Emerging-market assets rallied on China's tech support (Bloomberg, [Jul 21]), so the equity channel to EM is real, but the macro channels have not changed. China keeps importing iron ore heavily (Mining.com.au, [Jul 21]) even with property investment down 18%, because surplus steel is exported: Indian steelmakers are pivoting home as China squeezes margins (Reuters, [Jul 21]). That supports iron ore and AUD for now while pressuring steel producers from India to Europe, and an export-led 50.3 PMI keeps European exporters exposed to the curbs Paris and Berlin are aligning on. A real lift to Asian and commodity demand still needs household and private credit to turn.

Macro Stance: The BoJ is in active tightening mode with rates already at a 31-year high, and the yen has hit a 40-year low — creating a monetary policy paradox where even hiking hasn't arrested currency weakness. The BoJ has now signaled openness to *faster* rate hikes, a material hawkish escalation.

New / Most Important: This is structurally significant. Multiple sources confirmed today that BoJ officials view recent yen weakness as an upside inflation risk and are "open to raising rates faster" than previously communicated. Japan's Ministry of Finance stated readiness for "decisive currency action" — verbal intervention that historically precedes actual FX intervention. The 40-year yen low occurring simultaneously with 31-year high interest rates is an extraordinary divergence that reveals just how powerful the carry-trade structural short on the yen has become. The yen is being used as a global funding currency at such scale that domestic rate hikes alone cannot overcome the flow dynamics. If the BoJ accelerates hikes AND the MoF intervenes simultaneously, we could see a violent yen short-squeeze that reverberates through global risk assets — reminiscent of the August 2024 episode but potentially larger given the carry positions are more extended. This is the single most important cross-border capital flow risk on the board today. Global macro funds should be actively stress-testing their yen-funded carry book exposure.

Playbook ✓: BoJ tightening into yen weakness is consensus.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The *pace* signal is the break — "faster hikes" was not in the market's base case. Combined with intervention threats, this creates a non-linear yen recovery risk.

Macro Stance: The RBA is now in a hawkish posture with rate *hike* probability reportedly doubling due to the US-Iran war driving fuel prices higher. The AUD has strengthened above 0.7000 on this hawkish stance. Inflation remains the top concern for Australians per a new RBA community survey.

New / Most Important: This is a significant regime shift. While most DM central banks are debating the pace of easing or holding, the RBA is now actively warned by analysts as potentially *hiking* — making Australia a hawkish outlier in the G10. The energy supply shock from US-Iran conflict is the catalyst, transmitting through fuel costs into an economy where inflation was already sticky. The RBA's new community survey revealing inflation as Australians' top concern gives the central bank political cover to tighten further. This divergence creates a long-AUD trade thesis against currencies where central banks are easing. The AUD above 0.70 reflects this, and energy prices plus China's still-heavy iron ore buying support the terms-of-trade channel, even though China's property investment fell 18% y/y in January–June. Watch for AUD/JPY as the expression of this divergence — long the hiker against the currency where hikes aren't working.

Playbook ✓: Commodity-linked currency strengthening with oil surging and China still buying iron ore is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: A potential rate *hike* cycle restarting in a DM economy in H2 2026 is deeply contrarian relative to global consensus of synchronized easing.

Macro Stance: Wednesday's retail print closed the case for a strong second quarter. GUS reported June retail sales up 6.2% y/y in constant prices against a 5.2% consensus (Do Rzeczy, Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Jul 22]), with one category up almost 15% (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 22]); Bankier says the consumer has finally started to spend ([Jul 22]). ING BSK now puts Q2 growth at about 3.8% y/y (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 22]), with investment doing the lifting despite a consumption slowdown in ING's reading ([Jul 22]), on top of Monday's 7.6% industrial production (CEO Magazyn, [Jul 20]) and 5.9% wage growth (StockWatch.pl, [Jul 20]). The NBP released a new inflation projection (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jul 22]); Obserwator Gospodarczy's European comparison has Polish inflation down to 3% ([Jul 22]), while GUS's final June CPI is 2.5% (Rzeczpospolita, [Jul 15]). None of this settles the Council: a hawk told Gazeta Prawna the earlier cuts were premature ([Jul 21]), another member rates hikes more likely than cuts (Super Biznes, [Jul 21]), against Crédit Agricole's call for a 25 bp September cut to 3.50% (PAP Biznes, [Jul 20]). With refinery fuel prices still rising sharply (Super Biznes, [Jul 22]) and the end of the CPN package expected to lift July inflation (Gazeta Prawna, [Jul 15]), a hold is the base case.

Markets: Parkiet says a historic moment on the GPW is imminent, the WIG20 record within arm's reach with the index around 3900 points ([Jul 22]). PGE led Wednesday's gains (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 22]) and StockWatch.pl has the WIG and Orlen both at records with PGE, KGHM and Onde in play ([Jul 22]). Orlen's price is the highest in its history (Money.pl, [Jul 22]) and Bankier counts only 5 sector peers in Europe worth more ([Jul 22]). KGHM rose after June sales data (WNP.PL, [Jul 22]) a day after copper broke 13,600 dollars (Investing.com Polska, [Jul 21]). The card, which precedes Wednesday, has Orlen 149.16 (+2.2% 1W, +15.6% 4W), PGE 9.5 (flat / -2.4%), KGHM 306.45 (-4.1% / -12.4%), Allegro 45.08 (+2.6% / +15.8%), Dino 29.78 (+5.6% / +2.3%) with DNA Rynków noting the rebound extending above 30 zł ([Jul 22]), LPP 19950 (+1.5% / +8.0%), CD Projekt 230.9 (-0.3% / +1.0%), PKO 108.88 (-1.5% / +4.3%), Pekao 236.2 (-0.3% / +2.3%); EPOL closed at 41.32, up 1.3% on the week and 5.0% over four weeks. The zloty is caught between oil and the ECB: Bankier says crude is rising and the zloty stays under pressure though the euro is not climbing for now ([Jul 22]), MyBank.pl has EUR/PLN near 4.33 awaiting the ECB ([Jul 22]) and FXMAG asks whether 4.35 breaks after all ([Jul 22]). The card shows USD/PLN 3.7945 (+0.3% 1W, +1.0% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.3241 (flat / +1.1%). POLGB yields rose as the zloty firmed on Tuesday (FXMAG, [Jul 21]); no fresh bond headlines on Wednesday.

Fiscal & Politics: A day after Eurostat put public debt at 61.6% of GDP, the third-fastest rise in the EU (XYZ, [Jul 21]), Zero.pl notes Poland is also on the podium for its deficit ([Jul 22]) and Tysol.pl asks when Poland will double its debt ([Jul 22]). The politics run the other way: Money.pl's columnist calls the deputy prime minister's promise of a higher tax-free allowance "amok" ([Jul 22]) and Professor Orłowski told TVN24 the finance minister cannot block political pressure ([Jul 22]). The ministry tightens at the margins instead: lump-sum tax changes with identified losers (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 22]), a rental tax and higher lump-sum rates that INNPoland.pl says already chill entrepreneurs ([Jul 22]) and no public-sector pay rises for several years (Next Gazeta.pl, [Jul 22]). The government announced a tax on internet giants (INNPoland.pl, [Jul 22]) and Briefs Finance reports a US retaliation threat over it ([Jul 22]).

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen filled in its Q2 estimates: throughput of 9.17 million tonnes (Inwestycje.pl, [Jul 22]), less crude through its refineries and 1.9 billion zloty of write-downs (Bankier.pl, [Jul 22]), and it spent the day explaining the Ukraine fuel-price storm as a mix of price categories (Bankier.pl, Auto Świat, [Jul 22]) while a Skolim station undercutting Orlen reached the government spokesman (Wprost, [Jul 22]). KGHM's June copper sales rose 1% y/y and production 3% y/y (Inwestycje.pl, pb.pl, [Jul 22]), Poland stable and the US mine slumping (Energetyka24, [Jul 22]). PKO BP closed a synthetic securitisation of corporate loans that lifts its capital ratio (Bankier.pl, [Jul 22]). PGE proposed its own revision of the EU ETS (PortalKomunalny.pl, [Jul 22]) and 1.3 billion zloty is going into Poland's only underground power plant (Portal Samorządowy, [Jul 22]). Dino is suing a union leader (TOK FM, [Jul 22]) as unions allege illegal dismissals (PulsHR.pl, [Jul 22]), a day after opening its contested Wilanów store (Business Insider Polska, [Jul 21]). CD Projekt's Witcher 3 expansion gets its August gamescom showing (IGN Polska, [Jul 22]). Warsaw flat prices are falling (Subiektywnie o finansach, [Jul 22]) and rental listings dropped 3.2% m/m in June (PAP Biznes, [Jul 22]).

Geopolitics & Security: Belarusian commandos are at the Ukrainian border on Lukashenka's order (TVP Info, [Jul 22]), a day after Kosiniak-Kamysz warned Russia may use intercepted Ukrainian drones against Poland (Defense News, [Jul 21]). Poland is weighing a competing NATO offer for the MiG-29s promised to Ukraine (The New Voice of Ukraine, [Jul 22]).

New / Most Important: The 6.2% retail beat is the development: consumption is joining investment and industry, so the quarter is strong on every leg, while the government promises a bigger tax-free allowance with debt above 60% of GDP. For the RPP that is hawk fodder; for equities it is why Orlen and the WIG20 are at records. The oil shock via US-Iran raises energy import costs for Poland, and a consumer this strong lets the NBP extend the hold beyond what consensus expected.

Playbook ✓: Strong domestic demand with a 3900-point WIG20 and Orlen at all-time highs is the late-cycle textbook; stay with energy and the index leaders, keep the hold call.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Debt on the EU podium, a fiscal "amok" and oil-driven zloty pressure argue for wider POLGB spreads and a weaker currency, yet EUR/PLN is flat on the week and equities are at records; one side is wrong, and bonds are the side that has already started to move.

Macro Stance: Three distinct EM stories emerged this week. South Korea is experiencing a stock market boom but simultaneously trying to "tame market swings" with regulatory measures — analysts are skeptical of the intervention's efficacy. Vietnam's VN-Index plunged over 60 points in a sharp sell-off driven by three identified factors. Indonesia is accelerating market reforms to avert an MSCI downgrade — a serious structural risk for index-tracking flows.

New / Most Important: Indonesia's MSCI downgrade risk is the most consequential: a downgrade from EM to frontier status would force billions in passive outflows from EM-tracking funds. The reform acceleration signals urgency from Jakarta. Vietnam's sudden plunge warrants monitoring for contagion into broader frontier/EM sentiment.  |  Playbook ✓: Rising US yields and oil prices creating headwinds for EM is standard.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: South Korea booming while Vietnam plunges illustrates extreme EM dispersion — not a monolithic asset class.

Narrative: Mixed: the Nasdaq 100 at 29,154 is down 0.7% vs 4W while the S&P grinds higher, so mega-cap tech lags into earnings, yet AI capital keeps flowing, with Meta in talks for a $10B Anthropic deal.

Reported: IBM plunged 25% after its Q2 miss (TIKR.com, [Jul 15]) and reports in full today after its preliminary Q2 miss (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 21]). Pegasystems sank as Q2 results missed estimates by a wide margin (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 21]). Calix beat Q2 estimates on healthy revenue growth (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Dell — raised guidance by $27 billion and the Street is still catching up (TIKR.com, [Jul 21]). Synopsys — JPMorgan says its raised guidance is still too conservative (TIKR.com, [Jul 16]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The Nasdaq lagging the S&P while AI capex headlines peak is a yellow flag: either earnings re-assert leadership, or the narrative is loudest just as the marginal buyer is exhausted. Once broadsheets and government analysts frame AI as a systemic risk, institutions tend to de-risk quietly while retail keeps buying.

Narrative: Bullish: Alphabet reports today as the sector bellwether, with a Gemini delay and spending worries looming (Reuters, [Jul 21]). Meta's $10B Anthropic deal would position it as a fourth major cloud provider.

Reported: AMC rose 27% as strong earnings and record box office sales beat estimates (TIKR.com, [Jul 21]). Netflix's earnings forecast disappointed and the shares tumbled (Reuters, [Jul 17]). Publicis raised guidance on new business wins (WSJ, [Jul 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: Meta — BofA raised its price target on AI revenue potential (Investing.com, [Jul 20]); the Anthropic deal would re-classify it from ad seller to AI infrastructure platform. Alphabet — BofA also raised its target on cloud growth (Investing.com, [Jul 16]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The platforms' scorecard has flipped: for Alphabet, capex rather than cloud growth could decide the market's next AI trade (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]). A revenue beat can still be sold if spending grows faster.

Narrative: Bullish: rising yields and a +37 bps curve, 10 bps steeper than four weeks ago, are a modest tailwind, and NIM expansion is incremental rather than textbook. BlackRock and Goldman both made bullish US economy calls, and results keep confirming it.

Reported: Schwab beat estimates as retail investors piled into the market (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 21]), with record Q2 revenue of $7.1 billion (finance.biggo.com, [Jul 21]). Capital One topped estimates as credit losses fell and the Discover integration progressed (Quartz, [Jul 21]). Morgan Stanley posted record revenue and profit as equities trading surged 69% (CNBC, [Jul 15]).

EPS Upside Watch: Zions — analysts increased their forecasts after a better-than-expected Q2 (Benzinga, [Jul 21]). Goldman Sachs — Wall Street is raising expectations for Goldman and other banks after strong earnings (Barron's, [Jul 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Credit, the usual late-cycle crack, is improving: Capital One's results show positive signs on consumer health (Barron's, [Jul 21]) even as labour data weaken. If card losses keep falling, bank estimates are too low, not too high.

Narrative: Bullish: WTI at 86.30 (↑17.9% vs 4W) on U.S.-Iran strikes is a massive move, and China's crude imports at the lowest in nearly a decade confirm a supply shock rather than demand-driven pricing. Energy is the sector most directly catalysed by the escalation.

Reported: Equinor's profit soared on wartime oil and gas prices (Reuters, [Jul 21]). Halliburton beat estimates but tumbled on a tepid revenue forecast and a Middle East recovery warning (Reuters, [Jul 21]). TotalEnergies expects higher second-quarter profit on the war-related price rally (Reuters, [Jul 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: Chevron — screened as poised to beat Q2 earnings estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 20]). ExxonMobil — higher oil prices could boost its second-quarter profits by $5 billion (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Energy is both a war trade and an AI-infrastructure trade: data centres are constrained by power availability, not chips, so natural gas is the next AI bottleneck. Two independent drivers stacking means energy can hold premium valuations even if the war premium fades, and gas producers are AI beneficiaries without the AI multiple.

Narrative: Bullish: defence spending and AI power demand support industrials, with the NDAA in play, and BWX Technologies lagged despite strong nuclear and defence prospects. Results are confirming the cycle.

Reported: 3M boosted its annual profit forecast on a resilient industrial unit (Reuters, [Jul 21]). Northrop Grumman beat Q2 estimates and raised guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]), with a record backlog (ChartMill, [Jul 21]). Alaska Air narrowly beat as fuel costs stayed high (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 21]) and fell on short Q3 profit guidance (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Vertiv — raised guidance twice this year and the Street is still behind (TIKR.com, [Jul 21]). UPS — Evercore ISI raised its target to $117 on the revenue outlook (Investing.com, [Jul 21]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The fuel shock splits airlines by pricing power: United absorbed a $2.3 billion fuel hit and raised its guide anyway (TIKR.com, [Jul 18]), while Alaska posted a $76M loss amid an 85% spike in fuel costs (KING5.com, [Jul 21]). Premium demand, not jet fuel, decides who keeps earnings.

Narrative: Mixed: Tesla reports today with Elon Musk looming over the narrative as much as fundamentals, and the Russell 2000 at 2965.95 (↓0.3%) shows small-cap consumer names lagging. The swing factor is whether oil (↑17.9%) starts to show in spending guidance.

Reported: GM beat on earnings and raised guidance amid a 'resilient' consumer and pricing (CNBC, [Jul 21]), with North American profits up 43% (Automotive News, [Jul 21]). Hasbro beat on sales and raised its outlook on Magic: The Gathering growth (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 21]). Domino's revenue beat as its supply-chain business offset weak demand (ET BrandEquity, [Jul 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Ralph Lauren — Raymond James upgraded it on a stronger growth outlook ahead of earnings (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]). Amazon — Wall Street is raising its price target ahead of earnings (Watcher Guru, [Jul 16]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil is up 17.9%, yet GM cites a resilient consumer and some restaurant sales are soaring amid higher gasoline prices (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 21]). The fuel tax on spending is not yet in the numbers, so any damage is more likely to surface later through guidance.
Narrative: Mixed: staples should benefit from the geopolitical risk-off rotation, but a 10Y at 4.65% makes their dividend yields less compelling on a relative basis.
Reported: Conagra fell as guidance disappointed and it cut its dividend (Barron's, [Jul 15]); a $2 billion charge signals more pain ahead for the food industry (MarketWatch, [Jul 15]).
EPS Upside Watch: Coca-Cola — keeps outperforming expectations going into its report (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 21]). The sector — XLP's future earnings outlook is tilting up (Trefis, [Jul 17]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The defensive bid assumes pricing power, yet Conagra's cut and PepsiCo's stuttering turnaround as Americans rethink snacking (ET BrandEquity, [Jul 15]) say packaged food is losing it. Within staples, brands with volume, not the sector label, are what protect earnings.

Narrative: Bullish: CVS rose on improving execution and a better payer margin outlook, a sign pricing power is returning to managed care, and healthcare is a defensive beneficiary of the geopolitical risk.

Reported: UnitedHealth blew past estimates and hiked its earnings outlook as it reined in costs (CNBC, [Jul 16]). Danaher beat estimates but the stock dropped the most since 1991 (Barron's, [Jul 21]). Novartis beat on earnings, but cash flow weakened (TradingView, [Jul 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Humana — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Jul 16]), as UnitedHealth sees improving medical cost trends (Seeking Alpha, [Jul 15]). Pharma — Q2 arrives as the group picks up steam on dealmaking and policy tailwinds (BioSpace, [Jul 15]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Coverage loss cuts both ways: Intuitive tied Q2 procedure softness to ACA subsidy expirations (MedTech Dive, [Jul 17]), while insurers report lower medical costs. Fewer procedures are a provider and medtech problem but a payer tailwind, which favours managed care over device makers.
Narrative: Bullish: copper at 6.49 (↑5.7% vs 4W) tracks AI data-centre and grid-capex demand, while gold at 4153.70 (↑0.6%) holds its bid as the Iran conflict escalates.

Reported: BASF lifted guidance as higher chemical prices boosted earnings (Bloomberg.com, [Jul 15]). Steel Dynamics' upbeat Q2 was weighed down by aluminum losses (Manufacturing Dive, [Jul 21]). Lynas fell to a five-month low after a revenue miss (Mining.com, [Jul 21]).
EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners — pitched as the market's possible biggest comeback story (MarketBeat, [Jul 20]), with Atlas Mining turning profitable on higher gold prices (Inquirer.net, [Jul 21]).
